bib.title: A Survey on LLM Inference-Time Self-Improvement

question: How can LLM performance and efficiency be improved at inference time using only frozen parameters and no further training, and how are the existing methods organised?
contributions: A review of LLM Inference-Time Self-Improvement (ITSI) from three perspectives: Independent, Context-Aware and Model-Aided
The first taxonomy of these methods (Figure 2)
A discussion of challenges and limitations for future research

limits: Survey with no experiments or comparative numbers; no method is benchmarked against another.
Authors concede they cannot give exhaustive technical detail and cover mainly ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML and arXiv papers.
Scope is decoding, sampling, prompting, retrieval and model-guided decoding with frozen weights. It does not cover agent loops, reflection, or harness or weight self-modification.
Written Dec 2024, before most later test-time reasoning-model work.
API access limits: OpenAI Chat API returns only a partial distribution, so full-distribution methods are unusable there.
practices: Pick independent methods when you want no maintenance; datastore or model-dependent methods need updating over time (Sec 5).
Check how much of the probability distribution your API exposes before choosing a logit-level method (Sec 5).
Expect sampling-based scaling to cost more inference time than direct decoding changes (Sec 5).
Test constraint-enforcing decoding for fluency loss, because constraints compete with the model's fluency tendencies (Sec 5).
Analyse bias in self-improvement methods; explicit mitigation instructions in the prompt may reduce harm from zero-shot CoT (Ethical Considerations).

terms.definition: relying on the LLM’s own frozen parameters without additional training or parameter updating to improve performance and/or efficiency at inference-time

enhances performance with an external (often small) model
selects the output sentence that maximizes the expected utility over the set of translation hypotheses
Hard constraints are strict rules that must be adhered to in the output; soft constraints are flexible guidelines the model aims to satisfy but are not strictly enforced
